# Sirach Chapter 42 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 42 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 42 continues the shame catalog (vv. 1–8, linked to ch. 41), then pivots to the notorious "daughter anxiety" passage (vv. 9–14), before opening the great hymn to creation (vv. 15–25). The daughter passage is among the most difficult in Sirach — its patriarchal anxieties require no softening but clear rendering. The transition at v. 15 to creation theology marks a major structural shift and must feel fresh and elevated.

**Key decisions:**
- v. 14: The misogynistic climax of the section. Greek: "better is the evil of a man than a woman who acts well, and a woman bringing shame." SOPHIA does not soften; translates directly.
- v. 15: "I will now call to remembrance" — the personal voice signals the shift to the hymn.
- v. 18: "the deep and the heart" — both cosmic and psychological dimensions are present; retain both.
- v. 21: "from everlasting to everlasting" — strong scriptural echo (Ps. 90:2); retain.
- v. 24: "All things are in pairs" — the doctrine of cosmic complementarity is a key theme of the hymn; make it stand out.

---

**42:1** Do not be ashamed of these things, and do not show partiality so as to sin:

**42:2** the law of the Most High and his covenant, and judgment that vindicates the ungodly;

**42:3** settling accounts with a partner and with travelers, and dividing the inheritance of an estate;

**42:4** accurate scales and honest weights, and whether you acquire much or little;

**42:5** fair profit in dealing with merchants, and frequent discipline of children, and flogging a wicked slave until he bleeds.

**42:6** Where there is a wicked wife, a seal is wise; and where there are many hands, lock things up.

**42:7** Whatever you hand over to others, let it be by number and weight; and put everything given and received in writing.

**42:8** Do not be ashamed to instruct the ignorant and the foolish, or an elder judged by those younger than himself. Then you will be truly educated and approved before all the living.

**42:9** A daughter is a hidden anxiety to her father, and worry about her robs him of sleep: in her youth, lest she pass the flower of her age unmarried; when she is married, lest she be hated;

**42:10** while still a virgin, lest she be defiled and become pregnant in her father's house; when she lives with a husband, lest she prove unfaithful; or after marriage, lest she be barren.

**42:11** Keep a strict watch over a headstrong daughter, lest she make you the laughingstock of your enemies, a byword in the city and a reproach among the people, and shame you before the assembly at the gate.

**42:12** Do not look at any man for his good looks, and do not sit in the company of women;

**42:13** for from garments comes the moth, and from a woman comes a woman's wickedness.

**42:14** Better is the wickedness of a man than a woman who does good — and a woman who brings shame and reproach.

**42:15** Now I will call to mind the works of the Lord, and what I have seen I will recount. By the word of the Lord his works came into being.

**42:16** The shining sun looks down on everything, and the work of the Lord is full of his glory.

**42:17** Even to his holy ones the Lord has not granted power to recount all his wonders, which the Lord Almighty has established, so that the universe might stand firm in his glory.

**42:18** He searches out the abyss and the human heart; he understands every cunning device; for the Most High knows all knowledge, and he observes the signs of the age,

**42:19** declaring what has passed and what is to come, and disclosing the traces of hidden things.

**42:20** No thought escapes him, and not one word is hidden from him.

**42:21** He has set in order the magnificent works of his wisdom; he is from everlasting to everlasting. Nothing can be added to him or taken from him, and he has no need of any counselor.

**42:22** How beautiful are all his works — worth contemplating even to the smallest spark!

**42:23** All these things endure forever; they are preserved for every need; they are all obedient to him.

**42:24** All things come in pairs, one the counterpart of the other; he has made nothing incomplete.

**42:25** One thing confirms the goodness of another; and who could ever have enough of beholding his glory?
